A one-pixel source with a far exterior quadrilateral exercises replicated cubic taps when every sample resolves to one pixel.
A one-column source crosses both horizontal borders before a tall scalar crop rotates counter-clockwise.
A one-row source crosses both vertical borders in a wide scalar crop without post-warp rotation.
A two-pixel source uses phases immediately around integral coordinates to exercise scalar f32 cubic phase construction.
A narrow two-column source combines far replicated borders, perspective skew, and tall-result rotation.
A short nine-column source combines far replicated borders and a wide projective crop.
A larger interior scalar crop uses thirty-second phases and a non-affine lower edge without relying on replicated borders.
A wide larger source exercises a high horizontal output extent with cubic samples beyond every source edge.
A tall larger source exercises a high vertical output extent, replicated borders, and post-warp rotation.
A balanced all-side exterior crop carries strong but bounded projective skew across a square high-variation source.
A skewed medium source stresses a bounded non-affine lower edge with mixed interior and replicated cubic coordinates.
An exact five-by-seven pre-rotation crop stays just below the height-to-width 1.5 counter-clockwise rotation threshold.

purpose: developer-only OpenCV crop oracle; not a normal Rust test dependency
